source_evidence: A limit order is an order to buy or sell a security at a specific price.
answer: A limit order sets a price condition: a buy limit order can execute only at the limit price or lower, and a sell limit order only at the limit price or higher. A market order does not set that same specific price limit, so it may not protect you from buying at a higher price or selling at a lower price than you wanted. A limit order offers price protection, but it may not execute if the market moves past your limit before it can be filled.
